subtype: Types of laughter and social bonding [Expressing]
passage: Ganga, when I was a young engineer in a Punjab town, I sat with a seventy-year-old colleague, Mr. Grewal, who had the loudest guffaw I ever heard. When a clerk dropped the stamp pad, he let it rip and the whole floor laughed with him. I was shy and only chuckled behind my hand. Then I went to a firm in Japan for a year, and the same guffaw at a meeting made everyone glance up. I learned a soft laugh there. But at the sweet shop after work my colleagues finally laughed with me, belly and all, and we became friends that day. I'm Tushar, and I say laugh together, and mind the room.

qa.q: Where did Tushar work as a young engineer?
qa.a: Tushar worked in a Punjab town.

qa.q: What did Tushar feel about laughing loudly in Japan?
qa.a: Tushar was more careful there, having seen everyone glance up at the guffaw, and adapted to a softer laugh. It may also have been a bit of self-consciousness.

qa.q: What could a young person do about their own laugh in different places?
qa.a: Notice how others laugh in the setting and adjust the volume, while still letting real amusement out with people they trust.

qa.q: How did Mr. Grewal's guffaw affect the office in the Punjab town?
qa.a: It made the whole floor laugh with him, so his loud laugh brought people together there.

grounding: An elder recalls that chuckles and guffaws build closeness, and that a loud laugh is normal in one culture and bold in another.

subtype: Types of laughter and social bonding [Expressing]
passage: The power cut plunged the whole floor of the Manila call centre into darkness just as Jaya's shift was ending. A second later there was a loud crash. Gautam, her teammate, had knocked his chair over. Silence, then a small snort from Jaya, then Gautam gave a deep belly laugh, and soon the whole row was howling by the glow of their phones. Jaya hadn't laughed so hard in weeks. A senior manager walked in with a torch, looked at them, and started chuckling too. In the dark, with everyone clutching their ribs, Jaya felt closer to her team than she had all month.

qa.a: Gautam knocked his chair over in the dark.

qa.q: What was Jaya feeling as she laughed in the dark?
qa.a: Jaya felt amused and warmly connected to the team after a hard month. The shared laughter suggests closeness, but it may also have released some tension from the power cut.

qa.q: What could a manager do when a team is laughing after a stressful surprise?
qa.a: Let the laughter happen for a moment, laugh along if it feels natural, and then help the team get safe and back to work.

qa.q: How might the senior manager have seen the loud laughter?
qa.a: At first the manager just looked, then chuckled, which shows the loud, spontaneous laughter was taken as harmless and bonding.

grounding: A young adult's shared spontaneous belly laugh builds closeness, complicated by a power cut in a call centre.
